description: Table 5 is a two-row hyperparameter table for a machine-learning model, rendered as a plain black-and-white text table with horizontal rules above and below the header. The header row contains the leftmost cell "Model" followed by a single merged cell labelled "Hyperparameter configuration" spanning the remaining eight columns. The second row lists the model name "SVR" in the leftmost cell, followed by eight parameter-name headers: C, cache_size, coef0, degree, epsilon, gamma, kernel and tol. The third row is the data row: the model cell is left blank (shown only as a short horizontal dash/line), and the corresponding values read C = 4.98, cache_size = 118.85, coef0 = 0.63, degree = 4, epsilon = 1.87 × 10⁻⁴, gamma = 3.57 × 10⁻², kernel = ploy, and tol = 1.22 × 10⁻³. The kernel entry is printed literally as "ploy", which is presumably the polynomial kernel (likely intended as "poly"). No other models, no units, no error bars and no additional rows or columns are present. The table documents the optimised SVR configuration (obtained by Bayesian optimisation with ten-fold cross-validation, per the citing text) used to predict microhardness from the three key features {G, δ_Ec, D_Ec}.

observations.observation: Table 5 contains only one model row, labelled 'SVR'; the model cell in the data row is blank (a short dash/rule) beneath 'SVR'.
The printed hyperparameter for SVR are: C = 4.98, cache_size = 118.85, coef0 = 0.63, degree = 4, epsilon = 1.87 × 10⁻⁴, gamma = 3.57 × 10⁻², kernel = ploy, tol = 1.22 × 10⁻³.
The kernel entry is printed literally as 'ploy', i.e. a non-standard spelling, presumably intended as the polynomial kernel.
The table header merges the eight parameter columns C, cache_size, coef0, degree, epsilon, gamma, kernel, tol under the single label 'Hyperparameter configuration'.
No units, error bars, confidence intervals or additional model rows are printed anywhere in the table.
The caption states the table gives the hyperparameter configurations of the SVR model.
The citing text states the hyperparameters of each model were optimised using Bayesian optimisation and ten-fold cross-validation.
The citing text states the three key features {G, δ_Ec, D_Ec} were the input parameters and microhardness the output parameter for the models.
The citing text states SVR achieved the highest R² (0.85) and lowest RMSE (0.39) among the nine ML models compared, motivating the listing of its key hyperparameters in Table 5.
